/-!
# Erdős Problem 435

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/435](https://www.erdosproblems.com/435)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [HwSo24] W. Hwang and K. Song, *The Frobenius problem for Numerical Semigroups generated by
  binomial coefficients*. arXiv:2412.17882 (2024).
-/

namespace Erdos435

/--
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\neq p^k$ for any prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. What is the largest
integer not of the form
$$\sum_{1\leq i<n}c_i\binom{n}{i}$$
where the $c_i\geq 0$ are integers?

If $n=\prod p_k^{a_k}$ then the largest integer not of this form is
$$\sum_k \left( \sum_{1\leq d\leq a_k}\binom{n}{p_k^d}\right)(p_k-1)-n.$$
This was first proved by Hwang and Song [HwSo24]. Independently this was found in the comment
section by Peake and Cambie.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos435.lean"]
theorem erdos_435 (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (hpk : ∀ p k : ℕ, p.Prime → n ≠ p ^ k) :
    IsGreatest
      {m : ℤ | ¬ ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, m = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 n, (c i : ℤ) * (n.choose i : ℤ)}
      ((∑ p ∈ n.primeFactors,
        (∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (n.factorization p), (n.choose (p ^ d) : ℤ)) * ((p : ℤ) - 1)) - n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos435

reformulations.difference: Hwang–Song define the Frobenius number using the maximum of the nonnegative integers outside the generated numerical semigroup. Lean instead uses IsGreatest on a set of integers, expanding representability into an existential over natural-valued coefficients.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Natural-valued coefficients are exactly nonnegative integer coefficients. Each nontrivial binomial coefficient is at least 2, so 1 is unrepresentable. Consequently any greatest integer gap is positive; adjoining all negative integers to the nonnegative gaps does not change their greatest element. The full equivalence with a natural-number greatest gap equal to the displayed integer formula was proved as Review435.natural_frobenius_iff. The equivalence with the linked proof's additive-submonoid formulation was also proved as Review435.linked_statement_iff.

review.notes: The formula, summation endpoints, prime multiplicities, coefficient restrictions, and integer subtraction match the sources. Scratch proofs establish that the hypotheses are equivalent to having at least two distinct prime factors, hence n ≥ 6, and that every prime-power index in the formula lies in [1,n). Independent residue-based computations agree with the formula for every admissible n ≤ 80, including F(6)=49, F(10)=1043, and F(12)=989. /workspace/review/checks.lean compiles without errors or warnings; the equivalence proofs have only standard axioms. The website records PROVED (LEAN), consistent with the metadata. The exact linked proof contains no sorry or custom axioms and its statement was verified equivalent. Its original proof certificate was not independently rechecked: it targets Lean/Mathlib 4.29.1, and compiling it against the sandbox's 4.33.1 encounters version-dependent proof failures.
